description: We are students with computational science, math and engineering backgrounds. We are open to work with people from different backgrounds and we hope to learn new things during this experience. We appreciate hard working and motivated teammates.
summary: Space2Earth is an interactive 3D platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge that bridges the Moon, Mars, and Earth through data-driven analog matching. Driven by real mission datasets—including LOLA/MOLA topography, ground ice, cosmic radiation, SPICE-derived solar irradiance, and surface lithology—it harmonizes planetary conditions into ~55 km grid cells to match target sites on the Moon or Mars with both established terrestrial research stations and newly discovered Earth locations. The platform features bidirectional search, landing site suitability rankings, terramechanics gravity adjustments, logistics cost modeling, and consultation-ready reports. Because launching unvalidated hardware into space costs tens of thousands of dollars per kilogram and carries immense operational risk, Space2Earth empowers space agencies and private aerospace teams to de-risk missions on scientifically calibrated Earth testbeds before flight.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

Space2Earth is an interactive 3D web platform that matches target regions on the Moon or Mars with their closest Earth analogs, and vice versa. It works across three modes:

Space → Earth: Select any lunar or martian coordinates to identify the top 10 established analog research stations and top 10 newly discovered global sites.

Earth → Space: Pick any terrestrial location to find equivalent planetary landing corridors.

Landing Recommender: Ranks candidate landing zones by terrain safety, slope, solar power availability, and resources.

To ensure physical equivalence, planetary data is binned into standardized ~55 km footprints (Moon 2°, Mars 1°, Earth 0.5°) and evaluated by a versioned, auditable scoring engine. Users can generate shareable, print-ready Mission Consultation Reports with side-by-side scientific comparisons.

2. What benefits does it have?

De-risks Missions: Validates rover mobility, habitats, and ISRU drilling equipment in high-fidelity environments before flight.

Dramatically Cuts Costs: Testing on Earth costs less than 1% of in-space flight testing ($10,000–$1,000,000+/kg).

Expands Global Access: Identifies overlooked field testbeds outside traditional catalog stations for universities and emerging aerospace startups.

3. What is the intended impact?

Agencies (NASA, ESA): Accelerates site selection for Artemis lunar basecamps and Mars surface architectures.

Commercial Space & Academia: Lowers the barrier for private aerospace teams to field-test hardware.

Education: Engages students and the public through interactive 3D comparative planetology.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used?

Web & UI: TypeScript, React 19, TanStack Start, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, and shadcn/ui.

3D Graphics: Three.js and React Three Fiber (R3F) for interactive globes with surface and elevation layers.

Ephemeris & Analysis: Python 3 (spiceypy, numpy, pandas) using NASA NAIF SPICE kernels (de440s.bsp, pck00011.tpc, naif0012.tls) to compute solar irradiance across 12 synodic lunar months.

Testing: Vitest and Playwright for scoring accuracy and cross-device testing.

5. How is your project creative?

Bidirectional Planetary Matching: Works in both directions (Space ⇄ Earth) rather than relying on static tables.

Whole-Earth Discovery: Scans the entire globe to find new, uncataloged analog terrains.

Realistic Terramechanics: Applies gravity scaling only where physics demands it (weight, bearing capacity, and 0.166×0.166× / 0.38×0.38× mass-offload), rather than incorrectly altering soil friction angles.

Mission Logistics Modeling: Estimates transport distances and logistics tiers from key NASA Centers (JSC, KSC, MSFC, JPL, Ames).

6. What factors did your team consider?

Strict Data Integrity: Uses genuine spacecraft data (LRO LOLA, MGS MOLA, NOAA ETOPO, Gruber permafrost, MSL RAD, USGS lithology) with zero invented values.

Independent Scientific Criteria: Evaluates solar illumination and geochemistry as distinct criteria to preserve physical meaning.

Universal Accessibility: Completely open access with no logins required; consultation reports are encoded directly into shareable URLs.
